title: ui: conditional formatting accepts == on a list field, so the rule is stored and never matches
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36219 (PR #36441, the Studio CEL editor refuses `==` / `!=` on a list field while typing). The PR left this editor out of scope by the card's inspector ruling; L1 (7079169862) asked for a card. Filed by the seat. Parent: #36219.

## What happens

The view's conditional formatting editor (`ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx`, `scope="record"`) lints `record.FIELD` expressions but is not given the object's multi-value fields. A rule such as `record.tags == 'vip'` on a list field is accepted, stored, and then never matches any row, because a list never equals a string. No save-side check refuses that shape for conditional formatting either, so the author gets no word at any point.

## To do

1. Feed the editor the object's field definitions the same way #36441 feeds the Studio inspectors, so it refuses `==` / `!=` between a list field and a scalar while typing, with the same rewrite hint.
2. Decide with the seat whether the view save should refuse the same shape, so a rule written outside the editor is caught too.

## Acceptance

- In the conditional formatting editor, `record.LISTFIELD == 'x'` is flagged while typing with the rewrite, and a rule that does match (for example a membership test) is accepted.

Blocked-by: #36441

## Grade
p2 · area:ux · domain:ui. A stored rule that silently never applies.
